name: Dolomite legacy exchange submitRingsThroughDyDx approval drain
summary: The legacy Dolomite exchange's public submitRingsThroughDyDx decodes caller-supplied ring orders and, before any order is validated in settlement, pulls each signer's deposit through the TradeDelegate into dYdX accounts it operates as global operator. The attacker forged orders naming wallets with stale TradeDelegate approvals and withdrew their funds.
notes: The exploit needed two grants made just after deployment: the TradeDelegate authorizing this contract to move approved tokens (0x80a75caa) and SoloMargin ownerSetGlobalOperator for it (0x852a237b), which let it operate the victims' dYdX accounts. The later of the two sets the age (rule 8).

Victims are the 180 wallets whose tokens the eleven attacker transactions pulled into the contract; loss.mjs over them gives these three tokens. Earlier submitRingsThroughDyDx and SoloMargin operations through this contract (2020-2021) are ordinary relayer trades.
